narr: A large storm system stretching from the mid-Mississippi Valley northward into the Great Lakes region on September 2nd through September 4, 2022, along with an abundant amount of moisture resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across middle Tennessee. Due to slow storm motions and training of thunderstorms, heavy rain and areas of flash flooding were the primary threat during this event with impacts mainly felt near and south of Interstate 40. Several reports of flash flooding were received along with heavy rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches.
ev: A Facebook report showed flooding at the Brookwood Apartments in Columbia on West 7th Street and Academy Lane with several cars flooded. Damages are estimated for the flooded cars.

Heavy rain near Nolensville resulted in several inches of standing water in the subdivision near Burnt Knob Road and Stewart Creek Road. This same subdivision was impacted by flooding about 24 hours prior.
Heavy rain and flooding southeast of Smithville forced the closure of an intersection at Bright Hill Road and Hooper Road.
